seo.metaDescription: A histogram where every item is its own dot, stacked in bins along one value axis. Color the dots by threshold band and mark a target.

props.markdown: A histogram that keeps the items. Each row of your data is one dot, dots with similar values stack in a bin, and the tallest stacks show where most items sit. You can still point at a single dot: it has a name, a tooltip and an announcement of its own.

Use `DotHistogram` for the distribution of one value across many items, when the individual items matter as much as the shape: tickets by hours to the first reply, invoices by days overdue, jobs by margin. `binWidth` sets the width of a bin and `domain` the range. `target` draws a reference line with a label, and `calloutId` pins a pill to one item. `toneBy` colors each dot, with a `thresholds()` result for named bands (which also puts the band in the tooltip and the data table) or a function for anything else.

If the same items are measured more than once and you want to compare the measures, use [StripPlot](/docs/strip-plot): one row of dots per measure, with a median. If you want totals per period rather than items, use [WaffleColumns](/docs/waffle-columns): one column of dots per period, where a dot stands for a unit of the total.
With no `toneBy`, every dot has the accent tone. `value` and `label` are field names, `binWidth` and `domain` fix the bins, and `target` marks the 4-hour goal.

`toneBy` takes a `thresholds()` result: the breaks, a tone for each band and a name for each band. `bands.legend(values)` gives the legend items with counts. A result of `thresholds()` has methods, so this example is a client component.

`DotHistogram` is built on `Chart`, so it follows the same keyboard model as the other charts: it is a single tab stop, and tabbing in shows the first dot with its tooltip and announces it. Its dots form stacks, so it moves in two dimensions: `←` and `→` walk from bin to bin, `↑` and `↓` walk up and down the stack in a bin. `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last point, `Enter` or `Space` selects the active point when the chart has `onSelect`, and `Esc` clears the active point. `Esc` is only consumed when a point is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes. The widget’s description ends with a keyboard hint (“Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.”, plus “Press Enter to select.” with `onSelect`); `keyboardHint` replaces it, for example to translate it, and `keyboardHint=""` turns it off.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each dot the keyboard moves to. With `toneBy` set to `thresholds()` the band is read as the series and the position counts within the band, as in “Critical, 1 of 6, #5600, 3.1%”: the band, the position in it, the item’s `label` and its value. Without bands, or with a function, the series is left out. A visually hidden data table follows the chart with the columns Item and Value, named after the `label` and `value` field when they are strings, and a Group column when `toneBy` is a `thresholds()` result. `dataTable` renames the caption and headers, or turns it off.

The SVG and the HTML overlay are `aria-hidden`, so a `target` line and a `calloutId` pill say nothing to a screen reader. Put the same facts in the `title`, the `description` or the data, as both examples do with their counts.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
